text: Prediction on a test set of existing judgments is not the same task as predicting outcomes for a party mid-litigation, because the precise formulation of facts used by such models emerges only once the judgment has been issued.
citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Morgan A. Gray, The Evolving Role of Artificial Intelligence in Law (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5541658

isBasedOn.name: The Evolving Role of Artificial Intelligence in Law

abstract: for instance, a lawyer advising a client on the probable outcome of a court hearing—does not have access to the precise formulation of facts presented in a judgment, as this formulation emerges only once the judgment has been issued.

additionalProperty.name: scope_conditions
value: legal judgment prediction systems trained and evaluated on published judgments
